content.title: About
content.content: Vodka and tonic is a classic cocktail made of vodka, tonic water, and often a slice of lime or lemon. It is refreshing, slightly bitter, and suitable for parties as well as a relaxed evening.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tonic was originally used as a malaria remedy because of its quinine content.
The drink gained popularity in the United States in the 1970s as a lighter alternative to straight vodka.
The combination of tonic's bitterness and vodka's neutral flavor makes it an ideal base for adding herbs and berries.
Lime or lemon is added not only for taste but also to enhance the aroma of quinine.

items.title: Moderate consumption
items.content: In moderate amounts, alcohol can promote relaxation and improve mood.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Tonic water provides water and electrolytes, helping to maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Quinine in tonic has antioxidant properties.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive alcohol intake leads to health issues, including liver disease and dependence.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some tonic waters contain significant sugar, increasing the drink's calorie count.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Quinine can interact with certain medications, such as anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 50 ml of vodka over ice in a glass, add 150–200 ml of tonic water, stir gently, and garnish with a lime or lemon wedge. You can also add a sprig of rosemary or a few berries for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store vodka in a cool, dark place with the bottle tightly sealed. Keep opened tonic water refrigerated to preserve its freshness and flavor.
